Bill number: HB1163
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1019
 By White

 HOUSE BILL 1163

 By Stevens

 AN ACT to amend Chapter __ of the Public Acts of 2025
 (1st Ex. Sess. – SB 6001 / HB 6004); and
 Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 13
 and Title 49, Chapter 3, relative to education
 funding for public charter schools.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-103(d)(3), is amended by

adding the language "or public charter school" after the language "Explain how an LEA".

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-105, is amended by deleting

subsection (d) and substituting instead the following:

 (d)

 (1) The funding that a student generates pursuant to this section must be

 administered and allocated by the department to the LEA in which the student is

 a member for the duration of the student's membership in the LEA, except that:

 (A) The funding a student generates pursuant to subdivision

 (c)(3) must not be allocated to the LEA, but must be maintained by the

 department; and

 (B) The state share of the funding a public charter school student

 generates for an LEA pursuant to this section must not be allocated to the

 LEA, but must be allocated directly to the public charter school.

 (2) A student's membership in an LEA begins on the first day of the

 student's membership and ends on the last day of the student's membership in

 the LEA, except that the membership of a student who graduates early is

 extended to the student's expected graduation date for funding purposes.

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-316, is amended by adding the

language "or public charter school" after the language "LEA" wherever it appears in subsection

(c) and by adding the following as a new subsection:

 (f)

 (1) The commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller of the

 treasury, shall develop, revise as necessary, and prescribe a standardized

 system of financial accounting and reporting for all public charter schools,

 including appropriate forms or other documentation. This system must be

 designed to facilitate year-to-year and agency-to-agency comparison, as well as

 adequately indicating the sources and uses of all funds received by each public

 charter school. The commissioner shall review the fiscal public school records in

 all public charter schools to the end that the expenditure of funds, whether for

 current operation and maintenance purposes, capital outlay purposes, and other

 school purposes, are properly accounted for and safeguarded.

 (2) The commissioner may require public charter schools that receive

 allocations of state education funding pursuant to part 1 of this chapter or

 otherwise to comply with one (1) or more of the requirements established for

 LEAs in this section, as the commissioner deems appropriate or applicable.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-112, is amended by deleting

subsection (a) and substituting instead the following:

 (a)

 (1) A local board of education shall allocate to the public charter school

 an amount equal to:

 (A) The local student-generated funds for member students in the

 public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA

 pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title;

 (B) The average per pupil state and local funds received by the

 district in the current school year above those required by the TISA for

 each member student in the public charter school in the prior year;

 (C) The per student state and local funds received by the LEA for

 member students in the public charter school in the current school year

 beyond the prior year's membership; and

 (D) All appropriate allocations under federal law or regulation,

 including, but not limited to, IDEA and ESEA funds.

 (2) The department of education shall allocate directly to the public

charter school an amount equal to the state student-generated funds for member

students in the public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA

pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title.

 (3) Federal funds received by the LEA must be disbursed to public

charter schools authorized by the LEA by either joint agreement on shared

services by individual public charter schools or sub-grants to a public charter

school for the public charter school's equitable share of the federal grant based

on eligible students. The allocation must be made in accordance with the

policies and procedures developed by the department of education.

 (4) Each LEA shall include as part of its budget submitted pursuant to §

49-2-203, the per pupil amount of local money it will pass through to public

charter schools during the upcoming school year, including all calculations listed

in this section. Allocations to public charter schools during that year must be

 based on the calculated amounts. The LEA shall distribute the portion of local

 funds it expects to receive in no fewer than nine (9) equal installments to public

 charter schools in the same manner as state funds are distributed pursuant to

 chapter 3 of this title. An LEA shall adjust local payments to public charter

 schools, at a minimum, in October, February, and June, based on changes in

 revenue, student membership, or student services. All funds received by a public

 charter school must be spent according to the budget submitted or as otherwise

 revised by the public charter school governing body, subject to the requirements

 of state and federal law.

 SECTION 5. Sections 1 and 3 of this act take effect upon becoming a law, the public

welfare requiring it. For rulemaking purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this act take effect upon

becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it. For all other purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this

act take effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would change how public charter schools are funded and monitored, and when some education funds are directed to them. It would add references to public charter schools in specified provisions of Tennessee’s education funding and financial reporting laws. For funding under Section 49-3-105, the Department of Education would generally send student-generated funds to the local education agency (LEA) where the student is enrolled, but would keep funds generated under subsection (c)(3) and send directly to a public charter school the state share generated for that school’s students. A student’s membership would run from the first through the last day of enrollment; for funding, an early graduate’s membership would extend to the expected graduation date.

The commissioner, consulting with the comptroller, would establish a standard financial accounting and reporting system for all public charter schools. It would support comparisons across years and agencies and show the sources and uses of each school’s funds. The commissioner would review charter-school financial records to ensure funds are properly accounted for and safeguarded, and could require charter schools receiving state education funds to follow one or more financial requirements that apply to LEAs.

Under a revised funding formula, a local school board would allocate charter schools local student-generated funds based on the prior year, certain state and local funds above TISA requirements, funds for membership added beyond the prior year, and appropriate federal allocations. The Department of Education would separately allocate directly to a charter school the state student-generated funds for its prior-year members. Federal funds received by an LEA would go to its authorized charter schools through either a shared-services agreement or subgrants reflecting each school’s equitable share based on eligible students, under department policies.

Each LEA would have to include in its budget the per-pupil local amount it plans to pass through to charter schools and the calculations supporting it. The LEA would pay expected local funds in at least nine equal installments, in the same manner as state funds, and adjust payments at least in October, February, and June for changes in revenue, membership, or student services. Charter schools would have to spend funds according to their submitted budget or a revision by their governing body, subject to state and federal law. Sections 1 and 3 would take effect upon becoming law. Sections 2 and 4 would take effect upon becoming law for rulemaking, and otherwise on July 1, 2025.
</summary>

claims.summary_quote: send directly to a public charter school the state share generated for that school’s students
claims.source_quote:
The state share of the funding a public charter school student
 generates for an LEA pursuant to this section must not be allocated to the
 LEA, but must be allocated directly to the public charter school.
claims.rationale: This matches the direct-allocation exception.

claims.claim: A student's membership generally runs from the first through the last day of enrollment.
claims.summary_quote: A student’s membership would run from the first through the last day of enrollment
claims.source_quote:
A student's membership in an LEA begins on the first day of the
 student's membership and ends on the last day of the student's membership in
 the LEA
claims.rationale: Enrollment is used here as a plain-language description of the membership period.

claims.claim: An early graduate's membership extends to the expected graduation date for funding purposes.
claims.summary_quote: for funding, an early graduate’s membership would extend to the expected graduation date
claims.source_quote:
except that the membership of a student who graduates early is
 extended to the student's expected graduation date for funding purposes.
claims.rationale: The summary preserves both the exception and its funding-only purpose.

claims.claim: The commissioner must establish a standardized financial accounting and reporting system for all public charter schools.
claims.summary_quote: The commissioner, consulting with the comptroller, would establish a standard financial accounting and reporting system for all public charter schools.
claims.source_quote:
The commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller of the
 treasury, shall develop, revise as necessary, and prescribe a standardized
 system of financial accounting and reporting for all public charter schools
claims.rationale: The actor, mandatory action, and statewide charter-school scope match.

claims.claim: The commissioner must consult with the comptroller in establishing the system.
claims.summary_quote: The commissioner, consulting with the comptroller
claims.source_quote:
The commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller of the
 treasury, shall develop
claims.rationale: The bill expressly requires this consultation.

claims.claim: The financial system must facilitate comparisons across years and agencies.
claims.summary_quote: It would support comparisons across years and agencies
claims.source_quote:
This system must be
 designed to facilitate year-to-year and agency-to-agency comparison
claims.rationale: Both types of comparison are expressly required.

claims.claim: The system must show the sources and uses of each charter school's funds.
claims.summary_quote: show the sources and uses of each school’s funds
claims.source_quote:
as well as
 adequately indicating the sources and uses of all funds received by each public
 charter school.
claims.rationale: The summary accurately describes this reporting function.

claims.claim: The commissioner must review charter-school financial records so funds are properly accounted for and safeguarded.
claims.summary_quote: The commissioner would review charter-school financial records to ensure funds are properly accounted for and safeguarded
claims.source_quote:
The commissioner shall review the fiscal public school records in
 all public charter schools to the end that the expenditure of funds, whether for
 current operation and maintenance purposes, capital outlay purposes, and other
 school purposes, are properly accounted for and safeguarded.
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the review duty and its stated purpose.

claims.claim: The commissioner may require charter schools receiving state education funding to follow one or more financial requirements applicable to LEAs.
claims.summary_quote: could require charter schools receiving state education funds to follow one or more financial requirements that apply to LEAs
claims.source_quote:
The commissioner may require public charter schools that receive
 allocations of state education funding pursuant to part 1 of this chapter or
 otherwise to comply with one (1) or more of the requirements established for
 LEAs in this section, as the commissioner deems appropriate or applicable.
claims.rationale: The summary correctly presents this authority as discretionary and tied to receipt of state education funds.

claims.claim: The local school board must allocate local student-generated funding based on the charter school's prior-year membership.
claims.summary_quote: a local school board would allocate charter schools local student-generated funds based on the prior year
claims.source_quote:
A local board of education shall allocate to the public charter school
 an amount equal to:

 (A) The local student-generated funds for member students in the
 public charter school for the prior year
claims.rationale: The summary identifies the correct allocating actor, funding type, and membership year.

claims.claim: The local school board's charter-school allocation includes certain state and local funds above TISA requirements.
claims.summary_quote: certain state and local funds above TISA requirements
claims.rationale: The summary accurately identifies this component without purporting to reproduce its calculation.

claims.claim: The local school board's allocation includes funds for charter-school membership beyond the prior year's membership.
claims.summary_quote: funds for membership added beyond the prior year
claims.rationale: The bill includes a funding component for membership growth.

claims.claim: The local school board's allocation includes appropriate federal allocations.
claims.summary_quote: and appropriate federal allocations
claims.source_quote:
All appropriate allocations under federal law or regulation,
 including, but not limited to, IDEA and ESEA funds.
claims.rationale: The bill expressly includes this component.

claims.claim: The Department of Education must directly allocate state student-generated funds for a charter school's prior-year members to that school.
claims.summary_quote: The Department of Education would separately allocate directly to a charter school the state student-generated funds for its prior-year members.
claims.source_quote:
The department of education shall allocate directly to the public
charter school an amount equal to the state student-generated funds for member
students in the public charter school for the prior year
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the department's direct-allocation duty and the prior-year basis.

claims.claim: Federal funds received by an LEA must be disbursed to charter schools authorized by that LEA.
claims.summary_quote: Federal funds received by an LEA would go to its authorized charter schools
claims.source_quote:
Federal funds received by the LEA must be disbursed to public
charter schools authorized by the LEA
claims.rationale: The summary correctly identifies the receiving schools and authorizing relationship.

claims.claim: Federal disbursement may occur through either shared-services agreements or subgrants.
claims.summary_quote: through either a shared-services agreement or subgrants
claims.source_quote:
by either joint agreement on shared
services by individual public charter schools or sub-grants to a public charter
school
claims.rationale: Both authorized disbursement mechanisms are stated in the bill.

claims.claim: Federal subgrants reflect the charter school's equitable share based on eligible students.
claims.summary_quote: subgrants reflecting each school’s equitable share based on eligible students
claims.source_quote:
sub-grants to a public charter
school for the public charter school's equitable share of the federal grant based
on eligible students.
claims.rationale: The summary accurately states the subgrant allocation basis.

claims.claim: Federal allocations must follow department policies.
claims.summary_quote: under department policies
claims.source_quote:
The allocation must be made in accordance with the
policies and procedures developed by the department of education.
claims.rationale: The bill requires compliance with department-developed policies and procedures.

claims.claim: Each LEA must include in its budget the per-pupil local amount it will pass through to charter schools.
claims.summary_quote: Each LEA would have to include in its budget the per-pupil local amount it plans to pass through to charter schools
claims.source_quote:
Each LEA shall include as part of its budget submitted pursuant to §
49-2-203, the per pupil amount of local money it will pass through to public
charter schools during the upcoming school year
claims.rationale: The summary correctly states the budget disclosure requirement.

claims.claim: The LEA's budget must include the calculations supporting the local pass-through amount.
claims.summary_quote: and the calculations supporting it
claims.source_quote:
including all calculations listed
in this section.
claims.rationale: The bill expressly requires the relevant calculations to be included.

claims.claim: The LEA must distribute expected local funds in at least nine equal installments.
claims.summary_quote: The LEA would pay expected local funds in at least nine equal installments
claims.source_quote:
The LEA shall distribute the portion of local
 funds it expects to receive in no fewer than nine (9) equal installments to public
 charter schools
claims.rationale: The minimum installment count and equal-payment requirement match.

claims.claim: The local installments must be distributed in the same manner as state funds.
claims.summary_quote: in the same manner as state funds
claims.source_quote:
in the same manner as state funds are distributed pursuant to
 chapter 3 of this title.
claims.rationale: The bill expressly links the distribution manner to that for state funds.

claims.claim: The LEA must adjust charter-school local payments at least in October, February, and June.
claims.summary_quote: adjust payments at least in October, February, and June
claims.source_quote:
An LEA shall adjust local payments to public charter
 schools, at a minimum, in October, February, and June
claims.rationale: The required adjustment months and minimum frequency are correct.

claims.claim: Payment adjustments are based on changes in revenue, membership, or student services.
claims.summary_quote: for changes in revenue, membership, or student services
claims.source_quote:
based on changes in
 revenue, student membership, or student services.
claims.rationale: The summary lists the same adjustment factors as the bill.

claims.claim: Charter schools must spend funds according to their submitted budget or a revision by their governing body.
claims.summary_quote: Charter schools would have to spend funds according to their submitted budget or a revision by their governing body
claims.source_quote:
All funds received by a public
 charter school must be spent according to the budget submitted or as otherwise
 revised by the public charter school governing body
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the spending requirement and the actor authorized to revise the budget.

claims.claim: Charter-school spending remains subject to state and federal law.
claims.summary_quote: subject to state and federal law
claims.source_quote:
subject to the requirements
 of state and federal law.
claims.rationale: The summary retains the express legal constraint.

claims.claim: Sections 1 and 3 take effect upon becoming law.
claims.summary_quote: Sections 1 and 3 would take effect upon becoming law.
claims.source_quote: Sections 1 and 3 of this act take effect upon becoming a law
claims.rationale: The sections and effective-date trigger match.

claims.claim: Sections 2 and 4 take effect upon becoming law for rulemaking purposes.
claims.summary_quote: Sections 2 and 4 would take effect upon becoming law for rulemaking
claims.source_quote:
For rulemaking purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this act take effect upon

becoming a law
claims.rationale: The summary correctly limits this immediate effective date to rulemaking.

claims.claim: Sections 2 and 4 take effect July 1, 2025, for all other purposes.
claims.summary_quote: and otherwise on July 1, 2025
claims.source_quote:
For all other purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this

act take effect July 1, 2025
claims.rationale: The date and distinction from rulemaking purposes match.
